incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered: PD-INVOCATION-9123 (gpu-slab-alloc-failure) - automatic paging to #eng-oncall at 21:13 UTC

pagerduty: ALERT: High GPU memory allocation failures detected in pool 'dedicated-gpu-3' across 4 nodes. Symptoms: repeated CUDA error 77 (memory mapping), slab allocator churn, OOM-like evictions. Escalation policy: on-call -> secondary.

Emma Li: acked and taking the page. I'm on it, routing to ops playbook. Setting incident channel to this thread.

Sachin Patel: grabbing logs from affected nodes now. Seeing a lot of: 
```
E CudaAllocator: failed to map slab mmapped region: errno=12
W KVCache: evicting active entries to free pages
I ModelServer: falling back to smaller batch size
```
Not classic OOM, looks like slab allocator can't mmap new slabs. Might be hitting a ulimits or host kernel slab fragmentation.

Kai Nguyen: @Emma @Sachin if it's slab mmap fails we saw similar on older AMIs with kernel 5.15 and bpf-enabled telemetry. Can you check `dmesg` and the nvidia driver logs? Also confirm whether these nodes had any recent jittery network mounts (we had one with overlayFS thrash earlier).

Marta Ruiz: Customer impact: A few Dedicated customers reported 500/timeout spikes; Console shows surge in request latency on route `/v1/generate/dedicated` starting ~21:05 UTC. Auto-fallback was triggered for some requests to CPU workers but with a 10x latency penalty. Collecting list of affected org ids.

Emma Li: quick mitigation plan: 1) remove nodes from pool (drain) 2) restart inference pods after clearing nvdriver caches / unload modules 3) temporarily reduce global batch size via feature flag to avoid further slab pressure 4) open PD escalation if repages continue. Executing step 1 now.

Sachin Patel: draining node gpu-3-2 (10.20.5.8) - pod eviction log: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-3-2 --ignore-daemonsets --force
Evicting pod inference-runner-77b9c -> succeeded
Evicting pod kvcache-88d1f -> succeeded
```
Node still shows allocator errors after drain; attaching driver logs: 
```
[2026-03-14T21:07:44Z] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:82:00): 77, GPU memory map failed, mmap failed, 0x00000000
[2026-03-14T21:08:01Z] CudaAllocator: slab_alloc returned -1, attempting fallback
```
This aligns with slab/mmap failures not recoverable by pod restart alone.

Kai Nguyen: switching to mitigation B: disable KV cache in the runtime for affected model families (this will reduce memory pressure but increase cost). Emma, can you flip runtime flag `redwood.runtime.kv_cache.enabled=false` for tenant-facing route?

Emma Li: flipping flag for route `dedicated.*` now via console. Rolling update in progress. Route config change id: cfg-20260314-2116. Expecting ~30s to prop.

incident-bot: Configuration update applied: `redwood.runtime.kv_cache.enabled=false` (cfg-20260314-2116). Notifying runtime controllers.

Marta Ruiz: Noted customer impact: several requests that hit fallback are still failing intermittently. Logged initial impacted orgs: org-1012, org-2209, org-3340. Raising severity to P1 due to degraded customer throughput.

Sachin Patel: tried full driver unload/reload on gpu-3-2: 
```
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
# followed by systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service
```
Driver unload failed with "device busy" for gpu-3-1 and gpu-3-3. They have active DMA mappings from kernel side. Kernel indicates "out of address space" while trying to allocate pinned memory.

Kai Nguyen: Ok we need an orchestrated node restart if drivers can't unload. Plan: cordon + drain remaining affected nodes and reboot them one at a time to recover kernel slab state. Doing that now with staggered window to keep capacity. Emma/Kai coordinate with capacity manager to avoid cascading evictions.

Emma Li: I'm coordinating capacity: spinning up 2 warm CPU fallback nodes (capped) to absorb traffic while we reboot the 3 GPU nodes. ETA for capacity spinup ~2m. Also increasing throttle on non-critical batch endpoints.

Marta Ruiz: I've informed the 3 affected customers with a brief note: we're investigating GPU memory allocation failures and some requests may be slower while we mitigate; next update in 15 minutes.

Sachin Patel: after reboot of gpu-3-2 driver messages are clean, `dmesg` no longer shows Xid 77. `nvidia-smi` reports normal memory. Rebooted gpu-3-2 at 21:26 UTC. Checking GPU-slab counters: reduced back to baseline.

Emma Li: reboot gpu-3-1 at 21:31 UTC. Asking autoscaler to hold scale-down for 5m to let pods stabilize.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note appended: Emma Li acknowledged at 21:15 UTC, Kai Nguyen on-call escalation at 21:19 UTC.

Kai Nguyen: after two reboots, pattern looks fixed. I want to run a longer test: heavy synthetic allocation load to ensure no regression. Sachin, can you run the alloc stress test on a non-prod node? Use `cuda-alloc-stress --slab-size=16G --iter=1000` and capture kernel logs.

Sachin Patel: running alloc stress on staging node now. Will post results.

Marta Ruiz: update to customers: we have recovered nodes and mitigations in place; some requests were routed to CPU fallback. We're monitoring for 30 min and will follow up if anything else pops.

Sachin Patel: alloc stress completed with no failures on staging (kernel 6.1). Staging had newer kernel. Suggest we patch affected production nodes to the same kernel housekeeping patch and coordinate a maintenance window for the full pool.

Emma Li: agreed. Short-term post-incident actions (P1):
- Rebooted affected nodes (done)
- Disabled KV cache for dedicated routes (done)
- Increased fallback capacity and held scale-down (done)
- Customer comms sent (Marta)

Longer-term (P2):
- Patch production AMIs to kernel 6.1 variant to avoid kernel slab fragmentation
- Add monitoring for slab mmap failures (track Xid 77 and mmap errno)
- Improve driver unload tooling to force driver cleanup before rebooting
- Revisit KV cache mem growth heuristics and hard caps per node

Kai Nguyen: I'll create a follow-up ticket and schedule AMI rebuild with test plan. Assigning to infra-team.

Emma Li: handing off to Kai for next on-call window. I'll stay available for 30m for questions. If anything fires again, escalate to oncall-secondary.

Kai Nguyen: taking handoff. Thanks all. Closing PD incident for now but leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: RESOLVE: PD-INVOCATION-9123 has been resolved by user Emma Li at 21:45 UTC.

Marta Ruiz: adding follow-up notes to ticket, will draft customer postmortem and the external status page blurb.

Emma Li: quick timeline for the incident to capture in postmortem:
- 21:05 UTC - first errors detected (Xid 77)
- 21:13 UTC - PagerDuty auto-page fired
- 21:15 UTC - oncall ack (Emma)
- 21:19 UTC - Kai escalated and recommended node reboots
- 21:26-21:34 UTC - progressive node reboots and recovery
- 21:45 UTC - PD resolved, monitoring

Kai Nguyen: adding root-cause hypothesis: kernel slab/mmap fragmentation plus older driver interaction causing mmap failures under high KV cache growth. Recommend patch + KV cache caps as Emma suggested.

incident-bot: Thread flagged for postmortem and follow-up: tag=postmortem-required, severity=P1, incident_id=PD-INVOCATION-9123.

Emma Li: thanks everyone — great coordination. I'll convert this thread into an incident page in the tracker and ping infra for AMI rebuilds.

Kai Nguyen: handed off, closing thread in 30m unless new alerts.
